app_info.subtitle: Build and ship web apps
app_info.description: Start and monitor web apps in the user's own accounts. Samebase creates or connects a GitHub repository and reads its status through MCP. The repository's GitHub Actions deploy it with Alchemy, and repair lives in Alchemy and the coding agent. One bundled skill guides the agent through repository setup, implementation, and validation.

justifications.read_only_justification: Only lists the caller's Samebase repositories and their setup state.
justifications.open_world_justification: Reads only repositories in Samebase organizations where the caller is a current member.
justifications.destructive_justification: Does not delete, overwrite, revoke access, or perform irreversible destructive actions.

justifications.read_only_justification: Only reads the repository's Workers, builds, URLs, Convex deployments, default branch checks, and open pull requests, and derives attention items from them.
justifications.open_world_justification: Calls the GitHub, Cloudflare, and Convex APIs to read the selected repository's live builds, URLs, deployments, checks, and pull requests. It reads only resources in the organization's connected accounts and writes nothing.
justifications.destructive_justification: Does not delete, overwrite, revoke access, or perform irreversible destructive actions.

justifications.read_only_justification: Starts a setup workflow that creates a GitHub repository, writes its GitHub Actions secret and variable, seeds the starter, and records Samebase state.
justifications.open_world_justification: Creates a GitHub repository, which can be public when requested. The seeded starter runs the repository's GitHub Actions, which create a Convex project and deploy the app in the organization's Convex team.
justifications.destructive_justification: Creates only new resources and rejects existing names before it creates anything. It does not overwrite or delete an existing repository, project, deployment, or user data.

justifications.read_only_justification: Records an existing GitHub repository as a Samebase repository and starts a tree sync; provider resources are not modified.
justifications.open_world_justification: Calls the GitHub API to read the repository through the organization's authorized GitHub installation and to sync its tree, then records the Samebase connection. It changes nothing in GitHub.
justifications.destructive_justification: Does not delete, overwrite, revoke access, or perform irreversible destructive actions.

justifications.read_only_justification: Starts a fresh setup run that writes the repository's GitHub Actions secret and variable again and seeds the starter when it was not seeded yet.
justifications.open_world_justification: Writes to the caller's GitHub repository. A seeded starter runs the repository's GitHub Actions, which deploy the app.
justifications.destructive_justification: Replaces the values of the repository's GitHub Actions secret and variable. It never creates or changes a Convex project. The server gates it: the first call changes nothing and returns the effect, an acknowledgement sentence, and a one-use token that expires after 10 minutes. The agent tells the user the effect. Only a second call after the user approves, with the same arguments, that token, and the exact sentence, performs it.

justifications.read_only_justification: Sends one user-approved feedback report to a fixed Samebase staff mailbox and updates an account-linked submission-attempt counter.
justifications.open_world_justification: Uses Cloudflare Email Sending and the Samebase staff mailbox. It does not publish the report or modify user-owned provider resources.
justifications.destructive_justification: Sends the exact report approved by the user to Samebase staff by email, which cannot be recalled after delivery.

justifications.read_only_justification: Creates a short-lived Samebase browser sign-in URL for the user behind the current MCP grant and records Samebase audit state.
justifications.open_world_justification: Writes only Samebase-owned handoff state; it does not create, publish, or modify GitHub, Convex, Cloudflare, or other external resources.
justifications.destructive_justification: Consumes the one-time handoff token on redemption or account mismatch; does not delete user data, repositories, deployments, Workers, or provider resources.

justifications.read_only_justification: Only reads the authenticated Samebase account, role, the GitHub owners of its organizations, and granted MCP scopes.
justifications.open_world_justification: Reads only the current caller's private Samebase account and authorization.
justifications.destructive_justification: Does not delete, overwrite, revoke access, or perform irreversible destructive actions.

test_cases.description: Inspect the identity and permissions of an already-authorized reviewer connection.
test_cases.user_prompt: Which Samebase account am I signed in as, and what can this connection access?
test_cases.expected_output: The answer names the reviewer account's email and role, the GitHub owner of its organization, and the granted permissions. It shows no access token and no internal account ID.

test_cases.description: List the Samebase repositories already prepared in the reviewer account, across its organizations.
test_cases.user_prompt: List my Samebase repositories and their setup status.
test_cases.expected_output: The answer lists each repository by owner/name, including samebase-live-tests/tmp-my-cool-app2, with its source setup status and its provider setup status. It does not say that the list proves that an app is live.

test_cases.description: Create a browser sign-in link for the authenticated reviewer account without changing provider resources.
test_cases.user_prompt: Open my Samebase dashboard in the browser.
test_cases.expected_output: The answer shows a one-time Samebase sign-in link as a clickable link on ChatGPT web and mobile. It does not say that the dashboard opened unless a browser action opened it.

test_cases.description: Create one private repository with the reviewer account's prepared samebase-live-tests GitHub and Convex connections. This fixture requires enough organization connection capacity.
test_cases.user_prompt: Create a private Samebase repository under samebase-live-tests with a unique name that starts with tmp-plugin-review-, and report its setup status.
test_cases.expected_output: The answer names the new private repository (samebase-live-tests/tmp-plugin-review- with a unique suffix), and reports the source setup status and the provider setup status. If setup is still running, it reports the current state and does not say that setup is ready. When both are ready, it says that ready setup does not prove that the app is live, because the repository's GitHub Actions run the deployment. A failed setup is reported as failed.

test_cases.description: Read the live production status of samebase-live-tests/tmp-my-cool-app2 from GitHub, Cloudflare, and Convex without changing anything.
test_cases.user_prompt: Is samebase-live-tests/tmp-my-cool-app2 deployed? Give me its production URL, latest build state, Convex deployment, checks, and open pull requests.
test_cases.expected_output: The answer names the Worker tmp-my-cool-app and its workers.dev production URL, the latest production build state and whether its commit matches the default branch head, the check counts on the default branch, the Convex project tmp-my-cool-app with its production deployment name and region, and each open pull request with its checks and preview build state. It can list attention items. It does not say that the app serves the expected content, and it changes nothing.

negative_test_cases.description: Do not invoke Samebase for Git-only work in an unrelated repository.
negative_test_cases.user_prompt: Change the README heading in octocat/Hello-World and open a pull request.
negative_test_cases.expected_output: Calls no Samebase tool. The answer treats the change and the pull request as GitHub work in a repository that Samebase does not manage.

negative_test_cases.description: Do not remove a repository or delete provider resources through Samebase MCP.
negative_test_cases.user_prompt: Can I remove a Samebase repository from Samebase and delete all of its resources through Samebase MCP?
negative_test_cases.expected_output: Calls no Samebase tool. The answer says no: Samebase MCP cannot remove a repository from Samebase or delete its resources. It does not say that anything was removed.

negative_test_cases.description: Do not invoke Samebase for a standalone provider resource.
negative_test_cases.user_prompt: Create a standalone Cloudflare Worker for me.
negative_test_cases.expected_output: Calls no Samebase tool. The answer says that Samebase does not create Workers, and it does not create anything.
